person.name: Henry II, Holy Roman Emperor
person.summary: Henry II (Saint Henry) was Holy Roman Emperor from 1014 to 1024 and the last ruler of the Ottonian dynasty. Rising from Duke of Bavaria (995), he secured the German throne in 1002, became King of Italy in 1004, and was crowned emperor by Pope Benedict VIII in 1014. A pious ruler closely allied with the Church, he founded the Diocese of Bamberg, promoted monastic reform, and consolidated imperial authority north of the Alps. Dying childless in 1024, he was canonized in 1146.

events.title: Ottonian succession crisis; regalia dispute
events.description: Following Otto III’s death, Henry confronted the funeral procession near the Alps, demanded the Imperial Regalia, and imprisoned Archbishop Heribert of Cologne to bolster his claim amid rival candidacies.

events.title: Crowned King of the Romans at Mainz
events.description: Henry was anointed and crowned King of Germany (Rex Romanorum) by Archbishop Willigis, marking a pivotal step toward imperial authority without a traditional Aachen election.

events.title: Cunigunde crowned Queen of Germany
events.description: Henry’s wife, Cunigunde of Luxembourg, was crowned Queen at Paderborn, reinforcing the legitimacy of Henry’s new reign.

events.title: Anointed King of Italy
events.description: After campaigning against Arduin of Ivrea, Henry was anointed King of Italy, restoring German royal authority south of the Alps.

events.title: Alliance with Jaromír; Bohemia tied more closely to the Empire
events.description: Henry backed Duke Jaromír against Polish advances, effectively bringing the Duchy of Bohemia more firmly into the Empire’s sphere.

events.title: Foundation of the Diocese of Bamberg
events.description: To strengthen royal influence and support missionary work, Henry established the Diocese of Bamberg, transferring secular authority from rebellious marcher lands to ecclesiastical control.

events.title: Crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Benedict VIII
events.description: In Rome, Pope Benedict VIII crowned Henry as Romanorum Imperator, formalizing his imperial status after years of consolidating power north of the Alps.

events.title: Peace of Bautzen with Poland
events.description: Henry and Bolesław I of Poland concluded the Peace of Bautzen, ending a protracted conflict over border territories and stabilizing the Empire’s eastern frontier.

events.title: Third Italian campaign against Byzantine influence
events.description: Henry led an expedition to southern Italy to counter Byzantine advances and uphold imperial suzerainty, working in concert with Pope Benedict VIII.

events.title: Death; end of the Ottonian line
events.description: Henry died without an heir, bringing the Ottonian dynasty to a close. The German princes subsequently elected Conrad II, inaugurating the Salian dynasty.

events.title: Canonization as Saint Henry
events.description: For his exceptional piety and support of the Church, Henry was canonized by Pope Eugene III, becoming the only medieval German monarch to be declared a saint.

events.title: Birth of Henry II
events.description: Henry II was born into the Bavarian branch of the Ottonian dynasty, the son of Henry II, Duke of Bavaria, and Gisela of Burgundy.

events.title: Father deposed; Henry enters ecclesiastical education
events.description: After his father's failed revolt and exile, Henry was placed under ecclesiastical guardianship and educated in the Christian faith at Hildesheim and by Bishop Wolfgang of Regensburg, shaping his lifelong piety.

events.title: Restoration of Bavarian ducal status; Henry named regent
events.description: With his father restored as Duke of Bavaria after submitting to the regency of Theophanu, the young Henry was appointed regent over Bavaria.

events.title: Succeeds as Duke of Bavaria (Henry IV)
events.description: On his father's death, Henry was elected by the Bavarian nobles as Duke of Bavaria, ruling as Henry IV.

events.title: Marriage to Cunigunde of Luxembourg
events.description: Henry married Cunigunde of Luxembourg, forging influential ties in the Empire's western regions. The couple, noted for their piety, would later both be canonized.
